findings: The pilot is a location-shift result, not a validity result: L11 vs N moved scores by -7.945 with 14.4% leaf flips, slightly worse repeatability (86.8% vs 89.0%), and no HANNA gain. That pattern is a criterion shift with decision impact and no observed alignment benefit.

Four reused inputs cannot support a five-arm within-item factorial. Item-level clustering means the score drop and leaf flips may be one or two texts; the HANNA null and the 2.2-point repeatability gap are well within noise.

N vs L11 answers the product question (keep or drop the production prefix). L00 is the first diagnostic, not a co-primary arm: it separates length/attention from cue content. L10 and L01 are only warranted if L11 differs from both N and L00.

The 2x2 (origin x strictness) plus N is scientifically complete but product-overcomplete. Interaction tests on reused items will be underpowered and will multiply comparisons before any held-out confirmation.

Leaf-flip rate is a decision-impact / cost metric, not a quality metric. Validity requires whether flips move toward human order, HANNA, pairwise ranking agreement, and separation of known-quality strata. Mean-score harshness is not a success criterion.

Repeatability is a constraint (the prefix must not make the judge noisier) but is not a reason to ship. A harsher, slightly less repeatable judge with unchanged human agreement is a product regression.

An obviously fictional dog-authorship arm tests generic authorship salience versus AI-specific provenance. That is a mechanism question. It does not change the ship/kill decision for the byte-exact production prefix and is not needed on the smallest path.
recommendations: Use a sequential reused-then-held-out design, not a simultaneous five-arm study. Gate on validity and invariance, never on score mean.

Phase 1a (reused, within-item, repeated draws): N vs L11 only. Primary: HANNA / human agreement and pairwise ranking agreement with humans. Co-primary invariance: prefix should not change quality rank order of the same text. Secondary: item-clustered leaf-flip rate as shipping-cost, test-retest repeatability, and whether flips agree with humans. Pre-specify that a score drop without validity gain is a fail.

Do not treat the existing four items as confirmatory. Keep them as a fixed reused block for continuity, but add enough reused items to make the item the unit of analysis. Bound whether the -7.945 / 14.4% pattern is item-idiosyncratic before opening more arms.

Phase 1b (reused, only if 1a shows a validity change or material decision impact): add L00. If L11 ≈ L00, the production text is a length/verbosity confound; strip it. If L11 ≠ L00, then add L10 and L01 to attribute origin vs strictness vs interaction. Stop at the first arm that explains the L11 effect.

Phase 2 (held-out, single contrast): confirm only the surviving contrast (likely N vs L11, or N vs the active fragment) on new creative-writing items never used in the pilot. Same primary validity outcomes. Do not re-optimize for harshness or re-open the full factorial on held-out unless Phase 1 left a genuine origin-by-strictness interaction.

Skip the dog-authorship arm on the product path. Revisit it only if an origin main effect survives L00 and stakeholders need to know whether any surprising authorship claim, rather than the AI-origin fragment, is driving the shift.

Lock success as: no held-out HANNA/ranking gain plus non-trivial leaf flips → do not ship L11; validity-neutral score shift → prefer N or a length-matched inert frame; ship a fragment only if held-out human agreement or ranking validity improves without a repeatability loss. Report item-level intervals, not a four-item point estimate.
risks: Overfitting the four reused inputs and then 'confirming' a prefix that will not generalize; reused-first without a held-out kill-gate makes this likely.
Neutral replacements that are not semantically inert, so L00/L10/L01 fail as controls and mis-attribute length vs origin vs strictness.
Batching five prefixes on the same item introduces order, position, and cache/leakage effects that look like prefix effects.
Treating harshness as rigor: product and legal stakeholders may want the AI-origin/strictness frame even when it only lowers scores and flips leaves away from humans.
Construct contamination: the origin cue may cause the judge to penalize AI-associated style instead of writing quality, which can look like calibration while destroying the quality construct.
Multiple comparisons across five arms and many leaves without item-clustered inference; 14.4% flips can be a few leaves on a few items.
Running the dog arm 'for completeness' burns budget, adds a non-production cue, and invites interpreting a demand-characteristic effect as a reason to keep or rewrite L11.
output.summary: Do not run a five-arm within-item study, and do not add a dog-authorship arm. The pilot shows L11 vs N is a harshness/decision shift with no observed HANNA gain and no repeatability benefit; that is a validity-threatening criterion shift, not evidence the production prefix works. Smallest product path: reused N vs L11 gated on human agreement, ranking validity, and invariance (not mean score); add L00 only if that contrast moves decisions or validity; add L10/L01 only if L11 is not explained by length; confirm a single surviving contrast on held-out items. Skip dog-authorship unless a surviving origin effect still needs a generic-authorship control.
